name: The Tome of Divinity

angles.text: Paladins undergo this trial not with steel or combat prowess, but by offering selfless aid to the innocent, embodying the virtue of compassion central to the Holy Light.
The errand reveals the deep domestic scars left by the Scourge on human society and illustrates the mutual reliance between Stormwind and Ironforge.

faq.answer: John Turner is a human caretaker who runs an orphanage in Stormwind alongside his wife. He travels to Ironforge roughly once a month seeking supplies and charity from dwarven citizens and merchant guilds to support children orphaned by war.

aliases: why does john turner need cloth
faq.answer: Turner needs linen cloth so his wife back in Stormwind can sew warm clothes for the orphan children. Due to an influx of tradesmen and shifting trade throughout Azeroth, basic cloth supplies have become scarce and hard to acquire.
faq.q: Why does John Turner need linen cloth?

faq.answer: The children under the Turners' care lost their parents during the devastating assaults by the undead Scourge over the past decade. The Third War left many families shattered across the human kingdoms, leaving many youths without homes.
faq.q: Why are there so many orphans in Stormwind?

aliases: why is john turner in ironforge
faq.answer: Turner travels across the mountains to Ironforge to appeal to dwarven citizens and various trade groups for donations and supplies that are otherwise difficult to secure in Stormwind.
faq.q: Why did John Turner travel to Ironforge?

aliases: what does this have to do with the light
why do paladins do this quest
faq.answer: The Holy Light demands selflessness, mercy, and service to those in despair. Assisting an exhausted caretaker provide for war orphans serves as a test of humility and charity for aspiring paladins rather than a display of martial strength.
faq.q: How does helping an orphanage relate to the Holy Light?

faq.answer: Turner's expedition has been agonizingly slow and largely unproductive because local supplies are tight and few groups have stepped forward to provide aid, leaving him unable to return home until a shipment is secured.
faq.q: Why has John Turner's trip to Ironforge been so difficult?

sections.body: The Tome of Divinity presents an initiate walking the path of the Light with a trial not of weapons, but of charity. In the bustling halls of Ironforge, an emissary of mercy named John Turner seeks assistance. Turner and his wife oversee an orphanage in the kingdom of Stormwind, caring for children left parentless following the Scourge's catastrophic rampages over the past decade. His journey to the dwarven capital reflects the shared hardships of the Alliance's common people.
sections.title: Charity in the Great Forge

sections.body: Gathering provisions across borders is no easy feat. An influx of working tradesmen across Azeroth has strained local supply chains, making simple materials scarce. Turner's journey to Ironforge to appeal to civic groups and citizens stalled after weeks of minimal progress, leaving him without the linen cloth his wife requires to fashion clothing for the children. By stepping forward to supply the cloth without demanding repayment, a servant of the Light demonstrates the selfless devotion that underpins their sacred calling.
sections.title: The Scars of the Scourge

summary: The Tome of Divinity calls upon servants of the Light to perform an act of humble compassion in Ironforge. Assisting John Turner, who operates a Stormwind orphanage for children displaced by the Scourge, tests an initiate's commitment to selflessness and charity over martial glory.
